notes: Overview: Enterprise analytics + embedded insights provider. Evaluating generative stack to replace partial in-house LLM for customer support and structured extraction from claims documents.

Initial qualification (2025-11-20): customer needs: high-fidelity structured JSON outputs from tool chains, deterministic tool-calling for external enrichers, strict residency and KMS requirements. Target SLA: 200ms median per-token for UI flows, batch throughput for nightly extraction jobs.

POC scope (Dec 2025): 3 tasks — (1) chat support + tool calls (account lookup, billing), (2) structured extraction from claims PDF to canonical JSON, (3) reranking for KB search. Success metrics: >=95% schema conformity, <2% invalid tool invocations, latency SLOs for UI flows.

POC results (2026-01-10): Redwood hosted runtime delivered competitive latency and cost; however structured-output tests failed target. Redwood model returned malformed JSON or omitted mandatory fields ~18% of runs (target <=5%). Tool-calling failure rate ~6% (target <=2%). Incumbent (in-house) hit schema conformity 96%+, tool-calling 1% failures.
Quote from Eng lead (2026-01-12): 'We can't put this in front of customers if the extraction misses critical fields. The in-house model is just more reliable for our canonical schema right now.'

Security path: Redwood provided SOC2 report and KMS guidance. HSM/HW-backed key timeline pushed to >Q3 depending on product roadmap — flagged by StratusBridge security as blocker. They required audit logging with 13 months retention; Redwood's enterprise plan covered this but final attestation timeline slipped.

Procurement & budget: CFO instituted a hiring and spend freeze (email thread linked). Procurement paused additional spend while legal/infosec finish review. Final decision: exercise caution and continue with in-house stack to avoid integration risk and avoid multi-vendor complexity.

Competitive dynamics: Incumbent advantage = existing infra + better structured-output accuracy in controlled POC. Also lower perceived risk of SSO/KMS integration because incumbent already owns the tenant keys. OpenAI/Anthropic were evaluated by platform team as alternative but StratusBridge prioritized homegrown model for predictability.
